definitions.explanation: An overwhelming majority of a group. Emphasizes that nearly all members of a group share a characteristic, opinion, or behavior.

examples.japanese: {大多数|だいたすう}の{人|ひと}が{賛成|さんせい}した。
examples.english: The vast majority of people agreed.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}の{大多数|だいたすう}はスマホを{持|も}っている。
examples.english: The great majority of students have smartphones.

examples.japanese: {国民|こくみん}の{大多数|だいたすう}がこの{政策|せいさく}に{反対|はんたい}しているにもかかわらず、{法案|ほうあん}は{可決|かけつ}された。
examples.english: Despite the great majority of the public opposing this policy, the bill was passed.

notes:
Composed of {大|だい} (great) + {多数|たすう} (large number, majority).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大多数|だいたすう}の{人|ひと}: the vast majority of people
- {大多数|だいたすう}を{占|し}める: to make up the vast majority
- {圧倒的|あっとうてき}{大多数|だいたすう}: overwhelming majority

SIMILAR WORDS:
{多数|たすう} means "many" or "majority" without the emphatic force of {大多数|だいたすう}. {過半数|かはんすう} specifically means "more than half" and is used in voting contexts. {大多数|だいたすう} implies a much larger proportion than just over half.
